description: Energy-conservation drift benchmark per language: double-well potential integrated with velocity Verlet (symplectic) vs fixed-step RK4 (non-symplectic). Each language computes the same trajectory and reports relative energy drift vs the analytic E0; values are cross-language frozen invariants.

entries.name: double_well_verlet_rk4
entries.equations: V(x) = a*x^4 - b*x^2; F(x) = -dV/dx = -4*a*x^3 + 2*b*x; E = 0.5*m*v^2 + V(x). Verlet: velocity-Verlet kick-drift-kick. RK4: fixed-step RK4 on (x, v).

verlet_final_rel_drift.source: Frozen float64 result: velocity-Verlet on the double well at h=0.01, T=1000; Python and Octave bit-identical; Fortran agrees to ~1e-9 (Verlet) / ~1e-6 (RK4) relative because gfortran expands x**3 to multiplies while CPython/Octave use libm pow; rel_tol 1e-5 covers that honest cross-language spread without weakening the check (Verlet/RK4 drifts differ by ~500x). Symplectic drift is O(h^2) and oscillatory (max_rel 1.004e-4).

verlet_max_rel_drift.source: Frozen float64 max |E-E0|/|E0| over the full Verlet run; Python and Octave bit-identical; Fortran agrees to ~1e-9 (Verlet) / ~1e-6 (RK4) relative because gfortran expands x**3 to multiplies while CPython/Octave use libm pow; rel_tol 1e-5 covers that honest cross-language spread without weakening the check (Verlet/RK4 drifts differ by ~500x).

rk4_final_rel_drift.source: Frozen float64 result: RK4 on (x, v) at h=0.01, T=1000; Python and Octave bit-identical; Fortran agrees to ~1e-9 (Verlet) / ~1e-6 (RK4) relative because gfortran expands x**3 to multiplies while CPython/Octave use libm pow; rel_tol 1e-5 covers that honest cross-language spread without weakening the check (Verlet/RK4 drifts differ by ~500x). Non-symplectic local error accumulates, but stays ~3 orders below Verlet's oscillatory bound at this h.

rk4_max_rel_drift.source: Frozen float64 max |E-E0|/|E0| over the full RK4 run; Python and Octave bit-identical; Fortran agrees to ~1e-9 (Verlet) / ~1e-6 (RK4) relative because gfortran expands x**3 to multiplies while CPython/Octave use libm pow; rel_tol 1e-5 covers that honest cross-language spread without weakening the check (Verlet/RK4 drifts differ by ~500x).

entries.notes: Per-language energy-drift test (double well, x0=0.5, v0=0.4 stays in one well, E0<0). Verlet conserves energy to O(h^2) with bounded oscillation; RK4 shows smooth drift ~h^4-scaled at this horizon. Cross-language agreement is the check: identical invariants within rel_tol 1e-6.
